application_questions.question: A mobile plan in Melbourne charges $\$25$ per month plus $\$0.15$ per megabyte of excess data $d$. Write and solve an inequality to find the maximum excess megabytes $d$ so that the monthly bill does not exceed $\$52$.
A rectangular paddock has width $w\text{ m}$ and length $(2w + 5)\text{ m}$. If its perimeter must be at least $70\text{ m}$ and at most $106\text{ m}$, write and solve a compound inequality for $w$.

A school fundraiser in Geelong sells student tickets for $\$10$ ($x$) and adult tickets for $\$20$ ($y$) and aims to raise at least $\$600$. Write the half-plane inequality and state the boundary intercepts.

A lift in a Sydney office tower has a maximum safe load of $950\text{ kg}$. If an operator weighing $80\text{ kg}$ loads identical $30\text{ kg}$ crates, what is the maximum number of crates $n$ the lift can carry at once?

reasoning_questions.question: Use the number-line order of $-2 < 5$ to explain why multiplying or dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number reverses the direction of the inequality sign.
reasoning_questions.answer: Multiplying by $-1$ reflects numbers across $0$ on the number line: $-2 < 5$, but $(-1)(-2) = 2$ lies to the right of $(-1)(5) = -5$, so $2 > -5$.

reasoning_questions.question: Explain why the origin $(0, 0)$ is a convenient test point for shading a half-plane $ax + by < c$ when $c \neq 0$, and explain why another test point must be chosen when $c = 0$.
reasoning_questions.answer: When $c \neq 0$, substituting $(0, 0)$ immediately simplifies $ax + by$ to $0$, testing $0 < c$. When $c = 0$, the boundary line $ax + by = 0$ passes through $(0, 0)$, so $(0, 0)$ lies on the boundary rather than in either open half-plane.

application_questions.question: At a Melbourne bakery, $3$ meat pies and $2$ coffees cost $\$24$, while $2$ meat pies and $3$ coffees cost $\$21$. Set up and solve simultaneous equations to find the price of one pie $p$ and one coffee $c$.

A craftsman makes wooden chopping boards. His weekly cost is $C = 15n + 360$ dollars and his revenue from selling $n$ boards is $R = 39n$ dollars. Find the break-even number of boards $n$ and the break-even revenue.

A chemist mixes $x\text{ mL}$ of a $10\%$ saline solution with $y\text{ mL}$ of a $30\%$ saline solution to obtain $200\text{ mL}$ of a $18\%$ saline solution. Solve $x + y = 200$ and $0.10x + 0.30y = 36$ for $x$ and $y$.
The perimeter of a rectangular swimming pool in Brisbane is $64\text{ m}$, and the length $l$ is $8\text{ m}$ greater than the width $w$. Find the length and width of the pool.
application_questions.answer: $2l + 2w = 64$ and $l - w = 8 \implies l = 20\text{ m}, w = 12\text{ m}$

reasoning_questions.question: Explain geometrically why a system of two linear equations $y = m_1x + c_1$ and $y = m_2x + c_2$ has no solutions when $m_1 = m_2$ and $c_1 \neq c_2$.
reasoning_questions.answer: Equal gradients ($m_1 = m_2$) with different $y$-intercepts ($c_1 \neq c_2$) represent two parallel non-overlapping straight lines, which never intersect.

reasoning_questions.question: For the system $kx + 3y = 6$ and $4x + 6y = 12$, find the value of $k$ that produces infinitely many solutions, and explain what happens for any other value of $k$.
reasoning_questions.answer: Multiplying the first equation by $2$ gives $2kx + 6y = 12$. When $2k = 4 \implies k = 2$, both equations represent the same line (infinitely many solutions); for $k \neq 2$, the gradients differ and there is a unique solution $(0, 2)$.

application_questions.question: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining $A(2, 1)$ and $B(6, 9)$.
On a town planning grid in Canberra, a new bike path must pass through $P(3, -2)$ and run parallel to an existing road with equation $2x + y = 7$. Find the equation of the bike path.
Show by calculating gradients that the triangle with vertices $A(1, 2)$, $B(4, 6)$, and $C(8, 3)$ has a right angle at $B$, and find its exact area.
application_questions.answer: $m_{AB} = \dfrac{4}{3}$ and $m_{BC} = -\dfrac{3}{4}$, so $m_{AB} m_{BC} = -1$ ($\angle B = 90^\circ$); $AB = 5, BC = 5 \implies \text{Area} = \dfrac{25}{2} = 12.5\text{ units}^2$

application_questions.question: Find the value of $k$ such that the line passing through $(1, k)$ and $(4, 9)$ is perpendicular to the line $3x - 6y = 12$.
application_questions.answer: Line $3x - 6y = 12$ has $m = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $m_{\perp} = -2$; $\dfrac{9 - k}{4 - 1} = -2 \implies 9 - k = -6 \implies k = 15$

reasoning_questions.question: Explain why every point $P(x, y)$ on the perpendicular bisector of segment $AB$ is equidistant from $A$ and $B$ ($PA = PB$).
reasoning_questions.answer: Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$. For any point $P$ on the perpendicular bisector, $\triangle PMA \cong \triangle PMB$ by SAS ($AM = BM$, $\angle PMA = \angle PMB = 90^\circ$, and $PM$ is common), so $PA = PB$.

reasoning_questions.question: Explain why the perpendicular gradient formula $m_1 m_2 = -1$ cannot be used when one of the lines is horizontal ($y = k$) and the other is vertical ($x = h$).
reasoning_questions.answer: A horizontal line has gradient $m_1 = 0$ and a vertical line has an undefined gradient (division by zero), so the product $m_1 m_2$ is not defined even though the lines meet at $90^\circ$.
